proposal_text:
SIGNATURE: a check asserted to prove something without exercising what would falsify it. Seven instances across three VETOed iterations of plan-233-read-ledger-once (ledger #592/#593/#594, addendum #595). The highest-frequency and lowest-cost-to-close instance is V1: plan_grep_lint reported '0 citation(s) truth-checked' and exited 0 against a plan carrying nine Locked Decisions, because its _LD_HEADING_RE only scans regions under a 'locked decision'/'citation inventory' heading and the LDs were inline text. The lint recognized nothing and reported success. Read casually, the ladder looked clean.

COUNTERMEASURE (built, tested, in-repo): FailSafe/extension/scripts/check-plan-citation-parity.cjs compares the COUNT a truth-checking lint reports against the number of items that should have been checked, and fails on any mismatch, on an unobtainable lint output, and on a lint whose output shape no longer carries a count. Pinned by 11 behavioral cases in src/test/scripts/checkPlanCitationParity.test.cjs, including the origin case (three declared / zero checked must FAIL) and a partial-check case (two of three is not a pass) - the gate is proven to discriminate in the direction it guards, not merely to pass on clean input. Verified live against the real nine-LD plan: declared=9 truth-checked=9.

GENERALIZED RULE, for the portion not mechanically closable from this workspace: an exit code cannot distinguish 'I checked and it holds' from 'I did not recognize anything to check'; a count can. Every completeness claim must name the case that would falsify it AND show that case is reachable by the check as written - reachability is a separate question from assertion strength, and it is where four of the seven instances lived (unreachable via missing options, via fixture content, via a cast that neutralized the type, via a baseline captured from the thing under test). For multi-part claims, each part needs its own falsifying check; a proxy measurement of the easy half is not weak evidence for the other half, it is no evidence, and it reads as coverage.

UPSTREAM GAP, surfaced not filed (cross-workspace boundary): qor/scripts/veto_pattern.py emits severity-3 'repeated_veto_pattern' events, but qor/scripts/remediate_pattern_match.py PATTERN_RULES contains no rule for that event type (it covers aged_high_severity_unremediated, hallucination, regression, gate_override/orchestration_override, capability_shortfall only). Such events can therefore never be classified, never produce a proposal, and never be marked addressed - they accumulate unaddressed forever. Confirmed by running classify() over 7 unaddressed groups including this one: returned []. This is the same signature one layer up, in the governance tooling: a detector that cannot see the thing it exists to catch. It is also why this event had to be hand-authored rather than emitted and classified automatically.
closure_enforcer: cannot-automate: the PATTERN is an authoring habit (every completeness claim must name the case that would falsify it and show that case is reachable), enforced at /qor-audit Step 3, whose skill source is upstream and cannot be modified from this consumer workspace without install drift. Its highest-frequency INSTANCE is now mechanically closed and wired: npm run test:citation-parity runs scripts/check-plan-citation-parity.cjs --structure-only inside test:all, failing the build when any Locked Decision sits outside a heading plan_grep_lint scans - the exact V1 condition, detected with zero external dependencies so it holds in CI where qor-logic-plus is absent. Pinned by 20 tests covering every failure direction, verified green with the tool both present and absent. The residue is judgment plus an upstream PATTERN_RULES gap surfaced to the operator.

enforcement_evidence.verified: green with qor-logic-plus present AND absent; simulation confirmed to actually remove the tool
enforcement_evidence.form_fit_note: the four accepted closure_enforcer forms are qor-logic-centric (tests/test_*.py, qor.scripts.*, /qor-<skill> Step N, cannot-automate). None expresses 'a Node CI gate in a consumer repo', so cannot-automate is used for the pattern with the automated instance recorded here rather than overstating the form.
